# THEORYs with `tags` `causality`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds what the Anthology of the SOTA does not: reading whose subject no anthology topic can hold. The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Causality** — causation and the structure of causal relations — causal order, definite and indefinite, and its combinatorics, topology and geometry; sheaf- and process-theoretic accounts of causality; causal models, causal inference and interventionist accounts of what a causal relation is; and the metaphysics of causation — exclusion, mental causation, causal emergence and closure, reciprocal causation (ADR-035).

| [THEORY-058](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-058.md) v2 | Mental disorders are maintained by self-reinforcing causal loops rather than expressing a latent common cause, which is how they can outlast their triggers | Three traditions that do not cite one another for it put self-sustaining loops where a latent cause would be. Borsboom ([LIT-547](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-547.md)) makes disorder an alternative stable state of a strongly connected symptom network, kept up by hysteresis after its trigger has gone. Salkovskis, Sighvatsson and Sigurdsson ([LIT-538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-538.md)) make it a threat meaning protected by the behaviour it drives. Kendler ([LIT-539](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-539.md)) finds causal loops across levels, from genes to culture. The convergence is real; the evidence is indirect, simulated or clinical, and none of it is an individual time series showing hysteresis, so the account is Proposed. It says nothing about what starts a disorder. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-133](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-133.md) | A higher-level property is a cause in its own right, and its realizer is not, exactly when the effect would still follow had the property been realized differently; whether that holds is a fact about each causal system, not an a priori truth about levels | List & Menzies (2009), [LIT-722](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-722.md). Take causes to be proportional difference-makers. Then Kim's exclusion principle fails, and a revised one holds or fails system by system. A higher-level property excludes its realizer as the cause exactly when the relation is realization-insensitive. Proposed: the formal result is proved, but the claim that higher-level relations are typically insensitive is an observation about scientific practice, and Pernu disputes the paper's main example. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-138](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-138.md) | X is a cause of Y exactly when some intervention on X with respect to Y would change Y, where an intervention is an exogenous causal process that alone sets X (M1), affects Y only through X (M2), is not caused by anything that affects Y by another route (M3), and leaves Y's causes off the path through X unchanged (M4); so defined, causation is not reduced to non-causal facts but is not viciously circular, and needs no human agent | Woodward, "Causation and Manipulability" (SEP, 2001; revised 2023), [LIT-713](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-713.md). A cause is what changes the effect under a surgical, exogenous intervention, defined relative to the effect by M1–M4. The account separates total from direct causes by combining interventions, and treats natural experiments as interventions. Active as the standard the record uses for what a causal claim asserts. This statement says nothing about invariance, proportionality or levels. | Active |
| [THEORY-171](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-171.md) v2 | When the causal constraints on events depend on context, deterministic assignments that are causal in each context can fail to glue into one causal assignment, so causal structure is itself a source of contextuality | From Gogioso & Pinzani's trilogy: The Topology of Causality, [LIT-808](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-808.md), read in [NOTE-612](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-612.md), with the definitions of The Combinatorics of Causality, [LIT-800](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-800.md) ([NOTE-635](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-635.md)). Over a space of input histories with the lowerset topology, causal functions form a separated presheaf. It is a sheaf exactly when no two contexts impose incompatible causal pasts on a common event ("solipsistic contextuality"), and so always when the space is tight, as every space induced by a causal order is. The non-gluing example was checked here; the general theorem's proof was not read. It does not say any physical or quantum data display the effect. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-177](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-177.md) | In a binary cyclic system, the Contextuality-by-Default measure of signalling is twice the least total direct influence of context that any canonical causal model of the data must contain, and each content's share is the total-variation distance between its marginals | Wang, Sadrzadeh, Abramsky & Cervantes (2021), [LIT-851](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-851.md), Proposition 1. It joins CbD's maximal couplings ([LIT-777](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-777.md), Theorem 3.3) to Jones's 2019 correspondence between couplings and canonical models, which is quoted, not proved. The result measures signalling. It says nothing about contextuality, beyond the bound that a rank-2 system with Δ ≥ 2 cannot be contextual. The minimum is taken over models, so no particular causal model is identified. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-222](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-222.md) | A coarse-grained macro description can carry more effective information than the micro description it supervenes on, so the scale at which a system's causal structure is most effective can be a macro scale | Hoel, Albantakis & Tononi (2013), [LIT-1038](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1038.md), read in [NOTE-726](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-726.md). Effective information is effectiveness (determinism minus degeneracy) times the log of the state-space size, measured under uniform interventions. Coarse-graining always loses size and can gain effectiveness; when the gain wins, causal emergence CE = EI(macro) − EI(micro) is positive. Four toy systems give 0.40 to 2.92 bits. The arithmetic is exact. The reading that the EI peak marks where causation happens rests on imposing a uniform distribution at each level, which the paper adopts and does not test, so the account is Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-231](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-231.md) v2 | Within classical realism, a generalized-noncontextuality no-go refutes Leibnizian representations, not realist representations as such; it rests on a stronger assumption than a Bell-like no-go and so applies where none exists, as in prepare-measure scenarios, but only Leibnizianity implying noncontextuality is proved | Schmid, Selby and Spekkens (2020), [LIT-945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-945.md), §VI.C, §VIII (Eqs. 200, 214, 215), read in part in [NOTE-737](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-737.md), which is Skimmed: §§II–IV and the proofs in Appendices C–G were not read. A Leibnizian classical realist representation implies a generalized-noncontextual one, so every noncontextuality no-go is a no-go for Leibnizian representations. The converse is Conjecture 1′, so a Leibnizianity failure is not shown to be a noncontextuality failure. The prepare-measure claim is stated, not derived, in the text read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-243](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-243.md) | Interchange interventions on a fixed set of variables can be satisfied equally by different alignments related by a change of basis, so which internal direction is the mediating variable is fixed only relative to a chosen decomposition into units | Wu et al. (2024), [LIT-961](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-961.md), Appendix A, and Makelov et al. (2023), [LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md), Appendix A.3 and §8, read in [NOTE-809](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-809.md) and [NOTE-782](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-782.md). Both rotate the same three-unit identity network and find that the input aligns with h₃ in one basis and with (h₁ + h₂)/√2 in the other, equally well under interchange interventions on the input variable. Intervening on further variables separates them. Makelov et al. rest their verdict on component boundaries; the reply rests its on the interventions performed. Shown exactly for one constructed network only; that trained networks have many such ties is conjectured. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-275.md) | Directional information measures between two symmetrically coupled units follow the path of a recorded drive, not the symmetry of the coupling: flow reads two-way under moderate drive of one unit and one-way under strong drive | Das, Manikandan and Banerjee (2025), [LIT-947](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-947.md), read in [NOTE-788](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-788.md). Two colloids are coupled by the fluid through a symmetric tensor, and recorded noise moves one trap. Time-delayed mutual information and transfer entropy give drive → driven → other, with backflow at moderate drive. In numerics only, flow is one-way at strong drive. With no drive the coupled particles are independent at steady state. The paper does not test an unrecorded drive shared by both units, and it does not claim that the measures reveal coupling architecture. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-282](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-282.md) | A subspace intervention can reproduce the output effect of changing a variable without localizing it, by pairing a direction that varies with the variable but cannot reach the output with one that can reach the output but does not vary on the data | Makelov, Lange and Nanda (2023), [LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md), read in [NOTE-782](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-782.md). Proved for the construction (§3.2, Lemma A.1); shown in GPT-2 Small's MLP8 on IOI (46.7% FLDD, falling to 13.5% without the null-space component, 4.2% interchange accuracy) and in GPT2-XL MLPs on factual recall, where a residual-stream direction passes the same test. It does not say that subspace patching is unreliable in general, nor that a found direction with a null-space component is spurious: in a one-dimensional readout the test passes both kinds. The reply ([LIT-961](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-961.md)) contests the label, not the measurements. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-287](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-287.md) | Internal variables located by interchange intervention as mediating a language model's in-distribution behaviour predict whether its outputs stay correct under shifts that keep the task's mechanism better than output confidence or probes of the rest of the representation | Huang, Tao, Icard, Yang and Potts (2025), [LIT-987](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-987.md), read in [NOTE-765](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-765.md). In Llama-3-8B-Instruct over five tasks and ten shifts, counterfactual simulation is best on 8 of 10; a probe of the located variable beats a probe of its orthogonal complement on 7 of 10. Interchange accuracy and predictive power rise together only until accuracy nears 1. It does not say that the located variables are constitutive, that causal features always win, or anything about shifts that change the mechanism. | Proposed |
